author: ohtadmin
title: New programs await island students at N.K., Narragansett
text:
While some Jamestown teenagers will welcome a new principal next month, others will be able to enroll in a new vocational program at Electric Boat.
Tuesday is the first day of school for all Narragansett students and freshmen at North Kingstown, which are Jamestown’s co-high schools of record. The upperclassmen will return to Fairway Drive the following day.
There are 110 Jamestown students enrolled at North Kingstown for 2025-26: 28 freshmen, 23 sophomores, 27 juniors and 32 seniors. At Narragansett, 30 local students are enrolled across the four grades.
This year will be the first for Narragansett principal Conor McCloskey, who previously was the school’s assistant principal. He takes over the role from Christopher Fiore, who arrived in 2023 to replace Dan Warner. Fiore succeeded his predecessor when Warner retired after 20 years, and McCloskey worked with both men during his tenure as assistant.
“I feel very prepared and really excited to step into the role,” McCloskey said.
McCloskey said students can expect a continuity in leadership from Fiore’s tenure, including his presence at events and engagement with students. He also will help student-led decision-making on homecoming, spirit week and scheduling.
Narragansett offers career-technical education programs in agricultural science, information and computer technology, sports medicine and athletic training, educator preparation, mechanical trades, digital media production, and marine professions. The sports medicine program is new for this school year.
McCloskey said the goal of the program is “to make them successful after high school.”
“We really want to give students the options to pick the course work that interests them,” he said.
While most local teenagers attend North Kingstown, McCloskey said the students who choose Narragansett tend to do so because of its smaller size and the programs they offer.
“Students who come from Jamestown to Narragansett really get the opportunity to participate,” he said.
Aside from the new career-technical education program and McCloskey’s promotion to principal, other additions to Narragansett this year include a newly renovated computer lab, new furniture in the library and refurbished locker rooms. Gym teacher Jennalee Lopes has been promoted to serve as McCloskey’s assistant.
“There’s a lot of new things happening at Narragansett,” McCloskey said. “We’re really excited that students get to come here and get the continuity of great things from the past, and the exciting things that we’ll bring for the future.”
McCloskey said during the first day of school at Narragansett students will attend grade-level assemblies about new rules and policies. They also will attend their first classes, receive their syllabi and get to know their new teachers.
The school had a freshman orientation Aug. 25 when the new students toured the campus, participated in a question-and-answer session with seniors, met the counselor and nurse, received their technology items, and visited the career-technical education spaces.
At North Kingstown, only the ninth-graders and students new to the district will attend class on the first day of school.
Principal Shivali Finkelstein said Sept. 2 will be a transitionary day for them to become familiarized with the large campus. They will attend a two-hour orientation, receive their Chromebooks and meet their teachers. They also will be introduced to their advisory teacher, who they will have for all four years in the high school.
Finkelstein said Jamestown students may feel nervous coming into a larger school than the smaller tight-knit elementary and middle schools on the island. However, she said the special first day for freshmen is particularly helpful for those teens.
The school also collects feedback from new students in the middle of the year who explain how they feel about their new school.
“While they may not immediately get used to that environment really quickly, they do feel supported with the adults that they feel some connection, and they know who to go to, and how to get help,” Finkelstein said. “We have always tried to make that better each and every year for students and families.”
In addition to the orientation day, Finkelstein said the school organizations, including those composed of parents, teachers and students, will have an information night for families new to the district. That will be in September, but the exact date has yet to be determined. Some of the school departments also will participate in that event to answer questions about the school.
A machinist program will be offered by North Kingstown starting this school year. The program is in partnership with General Dynamics Electric Boat and previously was offered at the Community College of Rhode Island’s Knight Campus in Warwick.
Previously, North Kingstown students had to be transported to CCRI to participate in that program, but it is now being taught by Ryan Degre in the D Building near the campus. Seventeen students across all grades are enrolled in that program.
“That is a really new and exciting opportunity this year that we will be able to offer to our students,” Finkelstein said.
The machinist classes are also open as an elective for any student who wants to learn a skill even if they are not enrolled in the full program. The advanced culinary program also has been expanded at North Kingstown.
